quizzes.stem: A policy allows bedrock:* on * for an application's role. A reviewer asks for least privilege. Which rewrite fits?

options.a: Keep the policy as written and add a condition that requires SSL
options.b: Keep the wildcard action but name the single model's ARN in the resource
options.c: Replace the wildcard with a deny statement for every other model
options.d: List the one invoke action and name the single model's ARN

explanation.d: The page says to "grant only the permissions required to perform a task", by "defining the actions that can be taken on specific resources".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a wildcard action still grants more than "the permissions required to perform a task".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "By default, users and roles don't have permission to create or modify Amazon Bedrock resources", so a policy should add what is needed and not rely on denies.
explanation.a: Ruled out because conditions come after the basics: "defining the actions that can be taken on specific resources under specific conditions".

quizzes.stem: A service account must only call a Claude endpoint on Google Cloud. The team compares a ready-made grant bundle with one it authors. What does the page favour?

options.a: The tailored role with just the predict permission
options.b: A predefined role, since the platform maintains it for the team
options.c: A basic role such as Editor, since it covers every service at once
options.d: No role at all, since a service account works without any grant

explanation.a: The page says "custom roles are recommended because you create them, so you can limit their access to only the permissions that are required".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Predefined roles often contain more permissions than you need."
explanation.c: Ruled out because basic roles "provide access control to your Agent Platform resources at the project level, and are common to all Google Cloud services", which is broad.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "You grant access by assigning IAM roles to principals."

quizzes.stem: A team adds the deploy permission to its invoker role just in case. What does the Google page warn?

options.a: It blocks the predict permission until the deploy one is removed
options.b: It makes every prediction slower on the endpoint that holds it
options.c: It opens a route to exporting other models held in the project
options.d: It has no effect at all, because deploy only adds serving capacity

explanation.c: The page warns that the deploy permission "might allow a user to export other deployed or deployable models from the project".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the predict permission "grants the service account the ability to call the endpoint for predictions", and the page says nothing of speed.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the same sentence shows the predict permission grants "the ability to call the endpoint for predictions" on its own.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the warning is that it "might allow a user to export other deployed or deployable models from the project".

quizzes.stem: A project must keep Claude traffic in the EU and use Sonnet 5.5. Which Vertex endpoint setting fits?

options.a: The global value, since it keeps data inside the EU by default for everyone
options.b: The European multi-area value, since named places serve older names only
options.c: A specific region such as europe-west4, since it is the strictest choice
options.d: The us value, since Sonnet 5.5 is served there alone in this case

explanation.b: The page says a specific region serves `claude-sonnet-4-6` only and that the EU needs "the `eu` multi-region endpoint or a `europe-` region", so Sonnet 5.5 takes the multi-region value.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Global endpoints: Dynamic routing for maximum availability" says nothing of keeping data in a geography.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A specific region serves `claude-sonnet-4-6` only".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the rules say "Residency `eu` needs the `eu` multi-region endpoint or a `europe-` region".

quizzes.stem: A team asks AWS for 8 million input tokens per minute on Bedrock. What do the docs say about getting it?

options.a: It is within the self-service range, which reaches ten million
options.b: It is within the default, so nothing more is needed
options.c: AWS alone decides, since the quota is a Bedrock matter only
options.d: It exceeds the self-service ceiling, so Anthropic must approve it first

explanation.d: The page says "You can request up to 5 million input TPM and 500,000 output TPM without additional Anthropic approval", and 8 million is above it.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Default quota is 2 million input tokens per minute (TPM)." and 8 million is far above that.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the approval named is "without additional Anthropic approval", so Anthropic is part of the decision.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the self-service ceiling is "You can request up to 5 million input TPM and 500,000 output TPM", not ten million.

quizzes.stem: A compliance team wants a record of prompts and completions for Claude on Google Cloud. What do the pages advise?

options.a: Rely on Anthropic to hold the prompts for the customer
options.b: Switch on request-response logging for at least thirty days
options.c: Log the prompts alone, since misuse shows up in what users ask
options.d: Leave the platform's own defaults untouched and set nothing

explanation.b: The page says "Enable 30-day request-response logging of your prompt and completion activity to track any model misuse by your users."
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Turning on this service does not give Google or Anthropic any access to your content."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page asks for "prompt and completion activity to track any model misuse by your users", not prompts alone.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Anthropic recommends that you log your activity on at least a 30-day rolling basis", so the customer keeps the log.

quizzes.stem: A reviewer finds a single star in the resource field of a policy statement. Which practice rule does it break?

options.a: The document must carry the current version string at the top
options.b: Each entry must be a model ARN in a documented region, without wildcards
options.c: Every action must be one of the three invoke actions allowed
options.d: The statements must be allow statements and nothing else at all

explanation.b: The rule is "Every resource is a model ARN with a region from the Bedrock region list, the `anthropic.` model id form, and no wildcard."
explanation.a: Ruled out because that rule concerns the version: "The policy has the version `2012-10-17`", which a star in a resource does not change.
explanation.c: Ruled out because that rule concerns actions: "Every action is one of the three invoke actions".
explanation.d: Ruled out because that rule concerns the effect: "only `Allow` statements, and no `NotAction` or `NotResource`".

quizzes.stem: A reviewer sees the ready-made aiplatform user bundle attached to the calling service account. What does the practice require instead?

options.a: A custom role whose only permission is predict
options.b: The same bundle plus a deny for the deploy permission
options.c: A basic Editor grant scoped to one endpoint of the project
options.d: An organization-level predefined bundle with fewer permissions

explanation.a: The rule is "The Vertex role is a custom role (its `id` starts with `projects/` or `organizations/`, not `roles/`) whose only permission is `aiplatform.endpoints.predict`."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the rule asks for a role "whose only permission is `aiplatform.endpoints.predict`", and adding a deny leaves the bundle's extra permissions in place.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the rule requires a custom role "whose only permission is `aiplatform.endpoints.predict`".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the id "starts with `projects/` or `organizations/`, not `roles/`", and a predefined id starts with `roles/`.

quizzes.stem: A quota file asks for 6,000,000 input tokens per minute with anthropic_approval false. What does the review do?

options.a: It fails the request, since 5,000,000 is the unapproved ceiling
options.b: It passes the request, since the default is 2,000,000 already
options.c: It passes the request, since the output figure is under 500,000
options.d: It passes the request once the region has been named in it

explanation.a: The rule is "Without Anthropic's approval a quota request is at most 5,000,000 input tokens and 500,000 output tokens per minute."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Default quota is 2 million input tokens per minute (TPM)." is the starting quota, and a request may go higher up to the ceiling.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the ceiling covers both figures: "You can request up to 5 million input TPM and 500,000 output TPM".
explanation.d: Ruled out because only approval lifts the ceiling: "without additional Anthropic approval".

quizzes.stem: A project with residency us asks for endpoint us-central1 and model claude-opus-5-5. What does the review say?

options.a: It passes, since the global value always satisfies any residency
options.b: It passes, since the region begins with the us prefix
options.c: It fails, since a named location serves one older name only
options.d: It fails, since the region is spelled in the wrong form

explanation.c: The rule is "A specific region serves `claude-sonnet-4-6` only", and the model asked for is newer.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the prefix rule, "`us` needs `us` or a `us-` region", is met but is not the only rule.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the global value is "Dynamic routing for maximum availability", which says nothing of residency.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the spelling is fine: "`us` needs `us` or a `us-` region".
